fact_text: A green candle shows buying pressure and a red candle shows selling pressure, and the wicks show the price range that was rejected within the period.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Candlestick Patterns Explained | PSX Trading Strategy | Technical Analysis for Beginners' (YouTube, 2025-07-07)

fact_text: A bearish engulfing is a red candle whose real body covers the prior candle, with small wicks; the analyst said price tended to fall after one formed at a resistance zone.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Candlestick Patterns Explained | PSX Trading Strategy | Technical Analysis for Beginners' (YouTube, 2025-07-07)

fact_text: A bullish engulfing is the green mirror image of the bearish pattern; the analyst treated one forming at a support zone as a potential buying opportunity, with price moving up afterwards.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Candlestick Patterns Explained | PSX Trading Strategy | Technical Analysis for Beginners' (YouTube, 2025-07-07)

fact_text: The analyst said candlestick patterns matter most when they form at a support or resistance level, so the level should be identified before the pattern is read.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Candlestick Patterns Explained | PSX Trading Strategy | Technical Analysis for Beginners' (YouTube, 2025-07-07)
